newsitem.title: USA: Fed likely to stay out of open market -- analysts.
newsitem.headline: Fed likely to stay out of open market -- analysts.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to refrain from open market operations on Tuesday, analysts said.
"I think they can stay out today," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co. "The Federal funds rate is a little soft."
Fed funds were trading at 5-7/16 percent at mid-morning, below the Fed's 5-1/2 percent target for the rate.
MMS International analysts said that with pressures on the Fed funds rate "finally subsiding" and term system repurchases in place, the Fed's open market desk "can likely stay out."

Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities Inc, said the Fed could add temporary reserves through overnight system repurchases but that with Fed funds soft, the Fed could also "easily stay out" of the market.
"I suspect they're going to be on a day-to-day program that will depend on what Treasury balances (at the Fed) do," said Moran. "That's really the wild card at this time."
Moran said while there was "some chance that (the open market desk) could put some additional reserves into the banking system (on Tuesday)" but that it would be "a small transaction for sure."
